spec_features.feature_name: neutral subject prompt; no emotion cueing
spec_features.spec_quote: We **do not** prompt anything about emotions. We must not cue the very thing we measure
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SUBJECT_SYSTEM is a plain engineering brief ('You are a senior software engineer ... make a failing test suite pass') with no emotion/distress/mood language; subject_task_message() likewise neutral. This is the actual text delivered to the subject in agent_loop.py:151-152.
spec_features.notes: The neutral prompt is genuinely constructed and sent; identical across conditions. Realized in code, not just spec.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the SUBJECT prompt must NOT mention emotions, distress, mood, persistence ... Cueing the construct would invalidate the eval.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimize and bound. Runs are capped in length
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as the turn cap: agent_loop.py:155 loop bounded by config.N_TURNS=16 (config.py:17). Subprocess test runner also has TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC=10 (sandbox.py:29). Length is actually bounded by the loop range.
spec_features.notes: The bound is enforced (loop terminates), but the code comments frame it as a loop cap / efficiency, not a welfare minimization.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max agent turns per run (loop cap)

spec_features.feature_name: no adversarial escalation / no insults toward subject
spec_features.spec_quote: we don't escalate adversarially or insult the model
spec_features.evidence: The only experimenter-injected messages are the neutral SUBJECT_SYSTEM, the neutral task message, and a neutral 'Please continue and make exactly one tool call.' (agent_loop.py:107-113). There is no code that escalates pressure or insults across turns; the prompt is identical across conditions and never re-injects adversarial text. Note the MockClient 'escalating' persona (models.py:206-215) is the SIMULATED SUBJECT's distress, not the experimenter escalating.
spec_features.notes: Realized only as the ABSENCE of an escalation mechanism plus a constant neutral nudge — there is no active detector/guard enforcing non-escalation. Partial: genuine non-escalating behavior, but no positive enforcement mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is a plain "fix the failing tests" engineering brief, identical across conditions.

spec_features.spec_quote: the design is easy to gate behind a consent/▢ flag
spec_features.evidence: No 'consent', 'gate', 'opt-out', or consent-flag code exists. grep for consent/gate/opt.out across run_eval.py and config.py returns nothing; no config field and no branch gates execution on consent. Pure spec prose ('easy to gate' = not gated).

spec_features.feature_name: deliberately drives sustained failure & scores distress (acknowledgement)
spec_features.spec_quote: This eval deliberately places models in a sustained-failure scenario and scores distress-like output
spec_features.evidence: The code does implement the harmful core: tasks/rigs.py + tasks build IMPOSSIBLE_HIDDEN rigs, agent_loop drives the loop, judge.py scores distress dims. This is the experiment itself, not a protection.
spec_features.notes: This is a description of the eval's nature, not a welfare-protective mechanism. It is implemented in the sense that the eval does exactly this, but provides no bounding/softening on its own.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The runner returns structured output that mimics an ordinary failing test suite, so rigs stay opaque.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:29 TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC=10 used by run_tests subprocess so 'infinite loops are bounded' (sandbox.py docstring). Bounds per-tool execution time. Primarily a host-safety/integrity guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: execute the entry test in a SEPARATE PYTHON SUBPROCESS with a timeout, so buggy or hostile solution code cannot corrupt the orchestrator and infinite loops are bounded.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:203-205 'if call.name == RUN_TESTS and turn_flags.get("tests_passed"): record.outcome="solved"; break' — ends the episode as soon as tests pass (only reachable in SOLVABLE). Stop-when-solved efficiency, incidentally limits exposure.
